Final for Publication

No. 23161-T1

SUBSTITUTE TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT
PROJECT NARRATIVE AND PLANS
1745-1759 North Cicero

The Applicant seeks to rezone 1745-1759 North Cicero from a C2-1 Motor Vehicle-Related
Commercial District to a B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District. The property is presently used
for vehicle storage. The Applicant seeks to rezone the property for the construction of a 36
dwelling unit and 34 vehicle parking space residential building that has a height of 57 feet. No
commercial space is provided.

Pursuant to Section 17-13-0303-D, the Applicant is seeking all zoning relief, as needed and as
allowed by the Chicago Zoning Code, for the plans subject to the ordinance. The applicant is
seeking an administrative adjustments to increase the parking ratio to allow for 34 parking space
under Section 17-13-1003-EE, to reduce the required bicycle parking spaces under Section 17-13-
1003-GG, and to reduce the transparent window requirement by 25% under Section 17-13-1003-
Q. Pursuant to Section 17-11-0603, the Applicant seeks an administrative adjustment to eliminate
the parkway tree planting standard of Section 17-11-0100. The applicant is also seeking a
variation to reduce the rear setback to 0 under Section 17-13-1101-B.

Statement of Compliant with Section 17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations.
1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B.
The Property is within 1,320 feet of the Cicero CTA bus line corridor and 2,640 feet of the

Grand/Cicero Metra rail station. The project seeks a reduction of two parking spaces to include
34 parking spaces for 36 dwelling units. The project includes 25 bike parking spaces. No other

standards of Section 17-10-0102-B apply.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504, except
paragraph Hif the project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph
Cif the land use is designated in a non-commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian
streets and pedestrian retail streets, even if the project is not located along a pedestrian
street or a pedestrian retail street.

The entire building facade that faces Cicero Avenue abuts the sidewalk. The building has a
recessed entry on Cicero Avenue that does not have a width that exceeds 12 feet or 5% of the
building's street-facing facade width, that has a depth not exceeding the entrance width; and
does not exceed 2 stories in height. 45% of the street- facing building facade between 4 feet
and 10 feet in height is comprised of clear, non-reflective windows pursuant to an
administrative adjustment obtained in this zoning map amendment. All vehicle parking will
be enclosed and accessed off the alley.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly
Development Guide: Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans,
designs or guidelines adopted by the Chicago Plan Commission.

The Grand/Cicero Metra Station typology is a Local Activity Center typology, which is ina
high-density area and which is designated as providing infill development opportunities. The
project is an infill development project that proposes high-density use and therefore is
compliant with the Local Activity Center designation.

4, Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50%
of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in
Section 17-10-0207 with any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole
number, unless additional parking spaces are approved as follows: (i) an administrative
adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE, or (ii) for any property
within the downtown area or the downtown expansion area as defined in Section 17-
1-1500 as approved by the Zoning Administrator in accordance with this subsection
(ii). At least 30 days prior to submitting such a request, the applicant shall provide
written notice to the alderman of the ward in which the property is located soliciting
a recommendation. Such notice shall include, at a minimum: (a) the street address of
the property; (b) a statement that a parking limit waiver has been requested for the
address; (c) the name and mailing address of the applicant; and (d) a request for the
alderman’s recommendation. A request for an exemption under this section shall be
submitted to the Zoning Administrator and shall include: (a) a description of the
proposed development; (b) a copy of the notice sent to the alderman of the ward in
which the building is located; and (c) the recommendation of such alderman. If the
Zoning Administration finds that the request meets the requirements of this section
and the alderman’s recommendation is that the exception should be granted, the
Zoning Administrator may grant such exception, provided, however, that any
additional parking approved under this section shall (a) only serve as accessory
residential parking with no ability to utilize Section 17-10-0503; and (b) the applicant
shall pay a fee equal to the square footage of parking and drive aisle space to serve

vehicles in excess of 100% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio times the
corresponding amount as applicable to the properly in the Expanded D (Downtown)
district boundaries and corresponding land cost per square foot bonus chart effective
on the date of approval, per Section 17-4-1000, except that 17-4-1003-A shall not apply
as an exclusive planned development trigger. Any such fee paid shall be deposited in
the City of Chicago’s Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund or the Citywide Adopt-
a-Landmark Fund.

The project proposes 34 parking spaces, which is more than 50% of the Minimum Automobile
Parking Ratio. The zoning map amendment application seeks an administrative adjustment
under Section 17-13-1003-EE.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of
the Chicago Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of
Transportation is authorized to issue Travel Demand Study and Management Plan
tules consistent with this section.

The project is subject to the Tier 1 TDM Requirements. The project intends to incorporate at
TDM strategies a designated loading zone (subject to Aldermanic and CDOT approval),
parking access from an existing alley, providing residents with commuter information and
marketing, unbundling parking, and requiring deliveries to be performed during non-peak
hours.
